subject: NovaPay: elevated 5xx and throughput drop — urgent exec briefing
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@novapay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production errors — NovaPay inference 5xx + slow responses (us-west-2)

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike of 5xx responses and elevated p95 latency from your inference endpoint in our us-west-2 deployment at ~07:58 PST. Impact: ~12% of our checkout calls failed with 5xx and many timeouts — customers are seeing failed card tokenizations.

I attached a small log excerpt (support_log_excerpt.txt) and a short timeline. This is P1 for us. We are on a reserved capacity contract (D-2026-1078) and need immediate remediation.

Can you confirm what you see on your side and an ETA for a mitigation? If needed we can accept a temporary fallback to a smaller model, but we need confirmation on functional parity and should avoid any data/state loss.

Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Engineering, NovaPay
samir@novapay.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:25:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Production errors — NovaPay inference 5xx + slow responses (us-west-2)

Team — forwarding Samir's alert. Quick summary from our monitoring:
- We are seeing sustained token queueing and 5xx increase for NovaPay routes routed to dedicated pool d-pool-usw2-07.
- p95 latency jumped from ~160ms to ~420ms between 07:55-08:05.
- Error rate peaked at ~12% (5xx) and is still ~9% as of 08:20.

Customer: NovaPay (D-2026-1078) — reserved capacity. This is a P1 impact to their checkout flow.

Immediate asks:
1) Marcus — can you confirm whether this is saturation on the dedicated pool (GPU/slots) or a runtime regression?
2) Vivek — we need an exec decision on temporary burst capacity or model-fallback (billing/credit implications).
3) Marissa / Priyom — prepare CS/finance talking points and customer-facing ETA.

I'm attaching the first latency graph I pulled (nova_latency_graph.png). I'll keep the thread updated; if we need to escalate to the execs beyond this group please call it out.

Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

Attachments: nova_latency_graph.png (image/png)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Production errors — NovaPay inference 5xx + slow responses (us-west-2)

Sofia / Vivek — triage notes from infra (quick):
- d-pool-usw2-07 shows sustained GPU utilization at 98% across the fleet for the last 25 minutes. Memory pressure is low but NVLink saturation and kernel backlog observed.
- Runtime traces show heavy KV-cache churn for NovaPay's top prompt prefixes (large context reuse) which is causing blocking on continuous batching.
- Top model variant in use: redwood-1-large-8q. Fallback to redwood-1-medium-8q reduces per-request tokens and lowers per-token compute by ~30%, but we expect slightly lower throughput for a small fraction of high-complexity prompts.
- Cross-region reroute (us-east-1) would add ~60–80ms RTT — may still be acceptable for checkout staging but requires customer signoff for increased latency.

Immediate mitigations I can run now (non-invasive):
A) Enable short-term burst on d-pool-usw2-07 (+35% capacity) — requires admin approval to commit reserved headroom and will increase cost for the hour.
B) On-call can stage a model-fallback rule for NovaPay route to medium-8q (automated, reversible) — low risk to data/state.
C) Apply a conservative batching throttle to reduce blocking and prioritize low-latency tokens.

If we don't take action in the next 20–30 min, we risk higher 5xx and SLA breach. I recommend A + B as the stop-gap; A needs exec signoff (billing/credits) from Vivek.

Logs and quick trace snippet attached (small excerpt in thread).

— Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
marcus@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: NovaPay: elevated 5xx and throughput drop — executive decision required

Thanks for the quick triage. This meets the bar for executive intervention given reserved capacity SLA risk and potential revenue impact.

Decision (short):
1) Approve immediate burst of dedicated capacity in us-west-2 for NovaPay +35% for the next 4 hours — cost to be centrally approved.
2) Approve automated model-fallback to redwood-1-medium-8q for NovaPay routes until metrics stabilize.
3) Offer NovaPay a one-time incident credit (proposed 25% of last month’s committed spend) — CS/Finance to finalize.

Marissa / Priyom, please prepare the customer note and credit terms. Marcus, please proceed with A+B immediately and post operational updates here.

I am scheduling an exec sync at 11:00 to brief leadership and confirm longer-term mitigation (capacity ramp / workload partitioning). HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/1078

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
vivek@redwood.com

Samir

Date: 2026-11-29T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Post-action summary — NovaPay incident (us-west-2)

Quick post-action summary for the thread and execs:
Actions taken (timeline):
- 11:08 PST: Applied +35% short-term burst to d-pool-usw2-07 (approved by Vivek). See capacity_change_request.pdf attached.
- 11:12 PST: Rolled model-fallback rule for NovaPay traffic to redwood-1-medium-8q (automated, reversible).
- 11:20–11:40 PST: Applied conservative batching throttle and increased KV cache retention for NovaPay routes.

Immediate results (observed):
- 5xx error rate reduced from peak ~12% to 1.5% within 40 minutes of the changes.
- p95 latency improved from ~420ms to ~190ms.
- Throughput returned to expected baseline; no request re-ordering or state loss observed.

Customer comms:
- Marissa / Priyom: please send the incident summary and the proposed 25% credit offer. Samir / procure@novapay.com — we will provide the model-diff doc and an internal runbook for safe rollbacks by EOD.

Next steps:
- Root cause investigation (Marcus + infra) to complete initial findings within 48 hours; full postmortem in 7 business days.
- Product/R&D to assess model-variant memory and batching behavior for long-tail prefixes and recommend config changes to prevent recurrence.
- Finance to draft credit proposal and legal to confirm contract impact.

I’ll prepare the exec readout slides and share before the close-of-business. Thanks everyone for the fast coordination.

Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
